+# Maya Desai — Senior Platform Engineer onboarding plan
+
+Status: isolated onboarding workspace; access approval pending  
+Manager: Ethan Park, Engineering Manager, Platform Control Plane  
+Parent team: Platform & Console (`team/platform-console`)
+
+## Role and boundaries
+
+Maya will work across the LiteLLM inference gateway and Langfuse operations console. The team owns gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and operator-facing console behavior. Maya may design, implement, test, and review changes in those areas, but does not unilaterally approve production access, privileged credentials, security-sensitive behavior, customer-data handling, releases, or upstream publication. Runtime/kernel work, smart-routing policy, telemetry infrastructure, SRE operations, security/RBAC, product semantics, and enterprise-only licensed directories remain cross-team boundaries requiring the responsible owner.
+
+Ethan is Maya's manager and control-plane approver. Priya Natarajan is the Platform executive sponsor and escalation point. Proposed working mentors are Amara Diallo for API gateway/request validation/rate limits and Logan Wright (or a delegate) for telemetry/analytics boundaries; Ethan must confirm both pairings before they are treated as assignments. Security-sensitive access and behavior require Security approval; production-console access requires manager plus Security approval. [Team brief](../../curated/team-platform-console/brief.md) (`curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`); [employee directory](/knowledge/company/employee_directory.yaml) (`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`).
+
+## First week: access and safe local setup
+
+1. Day 1: complete SSO, security training, acceptable-use requirements, corporate email, Slack, and read-only team knowledge. Request GitHub organization membership and read access to LiteLLM and Langfuse. Do not request or use production secrets, customer-scoped data, KMS/HSM, org-admin, CI trigger, or deployment rights.
+2. Days 1–2: Ethan submits write-access requests for the two repositories with Maya's role and business justification. Standard GitHub access target is two business days; CI/CD rights begin only after training. Keep production-console access ungranted until the manager + Security approval gap is closed. [New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json) (`dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982`); [Cross-functional Access Provisioning](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/people-ops/crossfunctional-activation-access-provisioning-2028.json) (`dsid_9fc07b0c73ba41d9b984f6b485670d5d`).
+3. Days 2–3, LiteLLM: fork/clone without credentials in config files; create a conventional feature branch; run `make install-dev`, `make install-hooks`, `make help`, `make lint`, and `make test-unit`. For proxy work use `make install-proxy-dev`; DB-backed suites first require `make install-test-deps`. Use mocked unit tests and never real customer/model API credentials. [LiteLLM contributor guide](/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md) (`enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`).
+4. Days 3–4, Langfuse: install the repository-required Node/pnpm toolchain, bring up only the local development dependencies (`pnpm infra:dev:up`), generate/migrate/seed a local database, and run the affected package tests and lint/type checks. Use synthetic traces and prompts only; never copy customer prompts, bodies, outputs, or production exports locally. [Langfuse contributor guide](/code/langfuse/CONTRIBUTING.md) (`enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`); [Langfuse package scripts](/code/langfuse/package.json) (`enterprise_4e104191f0f9b715166144b0`).
+5. Day 5: pair with mentors to trace one synthetic request from LiteLLM routing/auth through Langfuse ingestion and console display. Produce a read-only architecture note and demonstrate local tests; no deployment or upstream PR.
+
+## Repository ownership and review routing
+
+- LiteLLM proxy, auth, policy/config, quotas, request validation, rate limiting, and gateway administration: Platform & Console; Ethan is the Redwood control-plane approver. Smart-routing or fallback policy also needs Mina Haddad's organization; telemetry contracts also need Logan Wright's organization; production reliability/runbooks need SRE.
+- LiteLLM provider adapters and upstream behavior: treat upstream maintainers as external owners. Redwood changes remain narrowly scoped, tested, and reviewed internally before any upstream proposal.
+- Langfuse `web/` console UI, API routes, auth, traces, sessions, scores, models, prompts, datasets, and eval UX: Platform & Console for Redwood integration behavior; product semantics need Product review, and auth/RBAC or outbound URL work needs Security review.
+- Langfuse `worker/` ingestion, queues, exports, retention, evaluation runners, and background jobs: Platform & Console plus Telemetry/SRE depending on capacity, data flow, and incident impact.
+- Langfuse `ee/` and `web/src/ee/`: separately licensed/enterprise-specific boundary; do not modify or redistribute without explicit owner/legal confirmation. [Code manifest](/code/manifest.json) (`enterprise_3923c6b386416268c7e7f382`); [Langfuse repository map](/code/langfuse/.agents/skills/langfuse-codebase-navigator/references/repository-map.md) (`enterprise_df926424cc402c9cb9aed210`).
+
+## Safe upstream issue handling and code triage
+
+1. Reproduce only with synthetic data in a local environment. Record version/commit, minimal steps, expected/actual behavior, sanitized logs, affected subsystem, and test evidence.
+2. Classify: support/configuration, Redwood integration defect, upstream defect, security/privacy concern, or reliability incident. Do not paste customer prompts, full bodies, model outputs, secrets, tenant identifiers, or unsanitized traces into tickets. Collect only necessary metadata such as timestamps, status codes, tenant-safe identifiers, SDK version, and request IDs approved for support use. [Support onboarding/triage playbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/onboarding-escalation-and-triage-playbook.json) (`dsid_92bc3577d2624a9cb294ab827ae60131`).
+3. Security/privacy suspicion: stop public discussion and normal upstream filing; notify Redwood Security immediately, preserve evidence under the incident process, and use the upstream project's private security contact only after Redwood Security approves disclosure. Langfuse directs security reports to `security@langfuse.com`; LiteLLM lists `support@berri.ai` for security inquiries. [Langfuse SECURITY](/code/langfuse/SECURITY.md) (`enterprise_d5cbe5168df3a0be47a0123c`); [LiteLLM security policy](/code/litellm/security.md) (`enterprise_dd1e0ebb4fcd33b86685309b`).
+4. Non-security upstream candidate: open an internal triage item first, obtain Ethan or delegated code-owner review, confirm license/data hygiene, search existing upstream issues, and draft the smallest reproducible report. Publication remains blocked until approval.
+5. Patch path: keep one problem per PR, add tests, pass local CI-equivalent checks, and document behavior. LiteLLM requires a CLA, at least one backend test, `make lint`, `make test-unit`, UI test/build checks where relevant, and targets `litellm_internal_staging`, not `main`. Upstream maintainers own final acceptance.
+
+## First 30 days
+
+- Days 1–5 — orient and validate: complete baseline access/training; map request flow; pass local setup checks; shadow support triage; confirm mentors and all approval owners.
+- Days 6–10 — bounded first change: select a documentation, test, or low-risk observability improvement with synthetic fixtures. Write a risk note and validation plan; Ethan approves scope before implementation.
+- Days 11–15 — integrate safely: implement behind existing boundaries, add focused tests, and run repository checks. Obtain gateway/console owner review plus Security, Product, Telemetry, or SRE review when the boundary map triggers it.
+- Days 16–21 — internal review: address feedback, demonstrate locally, and merge internally only if access and reviewers are satisfied. Target time to first merge is no later than 21 days, but safety and approval override the target.
+- Days 22–30 — operational readiness: shadow one support case and one rollout/readiness review; rehearse sanitized upstream triage; present a subsystem map and lessons learned. No independent production change, on-call primary duty, or upstream publication during the first 30 days unless Ethan and the required approvers explicitly authorize it.
+
+## Validation and exit criteria
+
+- Identity/access inventory shows least privilege; every privileged grant has owner, justification, expiry/review date, and approval evidence.
+- LiteLLM lint and unit tests pass; any UI change also passes UI tests and build. Langfuse affected-package tests, lint/type checks, and local service health pass.
+- Synthetic end-to-end trace proves gateway-to-console flow without customer data.
+- First change has focused tests, rollback/disable plan, internal code-owner approval, and any boundary approvals.
+- Maya can correctly classify and route a sample support issue, security report, upstream bug, and production incident.
+
+## Approval gaps (branch must remain isolated)
+
+- Maya's identity/start record was not found in the employee directory evidence and must be confirmed by People Ops.
+- Ethan must confirm the proposed Amara Diallo and Logan Wright mentor pairings.
+- GitHub write membership for LiteLLM/Langfuse is not evidenced as approved.
+- Security training, acceptable-use completion, and CI trigger eligibility are not evidenced.
+- Production console, production telemetry, customer scopes, cloud/VPN, secrets, deploy, on-call, and incident tooling remain unapproved; default is no access.
+- No authorization exists to publish upstream issues/PRs or to merge this personal branch into the team branch.
+
+## Evidence index
+
+- Platform & Console knowledge brief — `/knowledge/curated/team-platform-console/brief.md` (`curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`).
+- Employee directory — `/knowledge/company/employee_directory.yaml` (`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`).
+- Codebase manifest — `/code/manifest.json` (`enterprise_3923c6b386416268c7e7f382`).
+- LiteLLM contributor/security/architecture — `/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md` (`enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`), `/code/litellm/security.md` (`enterprise_dd1e0ebb4fcd33b86685309b`), `/code/litellm/ARCHITECTURE.md` (`enterprise_58d18d6180788880aa7e5faa`).
+- Langfuse contributor/security/repository map — `/code/langfuse/CONTRIBUTING.md` (`enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`), `/code/langfuse/SECURITY.md` (`enterprise_d5cbe5168df3a0be47a0123c`), `/code/langfuse/.agents/skills/langfuse-codebase-navigator/references/repository-map.md` (`enterprise_df926424cc402c9cb9aed210`).
+- New-hire access — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json` (`dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982`), `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/people-ops/crossfunctional-activation-access-provisioning-2028.json` (`dsid_9fc07b0c73ba41d9b984f6b485670d5d`).
+- Support data handling — `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/onboarding-escalation-and-triage-playbook.json` (`dsid_92bc3577d2624a9cb294ab827ae60131`).

+# Platform & Console codebase map: LiteLLM + Langfuse
+
+This map routes work to responsible Redwood roles. It is a review aid, not an access grant.
+
+## System connection
+
+LiteLLM is the OpenAI-compatible inference gateway, routing, and administration layer. It authenticates and validates requests, evaluates tenant/configuration policy, applies budgets/quotas and routing behavior, invokes model providers, and emits observability callbacks/OTel. The LiteLLM Langfuse integration converts gateway activity into Langfuse telemetry. Langfuse ingests events, processes queues/background jobs, stores/query traces and scores, and exposes the operations console for traces, sessions, evaluations, prompts, datasets, models, and administrative workflows. Both repositories are assigned to `team/platform-console`; SRE also shares both, and Performance & Evals shares Langfuse. [Code manifest](/code/manifest.json) (`enterprise_3923c6b386416268c7e7f382`); [LiteLLM Langfuse OTel integration](/code/litellm/litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_otel.py) (`enterprise_71a6a9dbc895e9c62ad3bfdd`).
+
+## Responsibility map
+
+| Subsystem / paths | Redwood accountable role | Required collaborators / review triggers | Evidence |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| LiteLLM proxy server, proxy API, tenant config and policy evaluation (`litellm/proxy/`, config repositories, admin endpoints) | Ethan Park, Engineering Manager, Platform Control Plane | Security for auth/RBAC/secrets; SRE for reliability/release | Employee directory (`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`); LiteLLM architecture (`enterprise_58d18d6180788880aa7e5faa`) |
+| LiteLLM API gateway request validation, rate limits and quotas | Ethan Park; implementation mentor proposed: Amara Diallo | Cole Summers for usage enforcement/billing hooks; Security for bypass or identity risk | Employee directory (`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`) |
+| LiteLLM routing, regional policies, automated fallback | Mina Haddad, Engineering Manager, Smart Routing | Ethan for control-plane integration; SRE for rollout/failure modes | Employee directory (`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`) |
+| LiteLLM telemetry callbacks and `integrations/langfuse/` | Ethan Park for gateway contract; Logan Wright for telemetry/analytics platform | Langfuse console/ingestion owner; Privacy/Security if payload content changes | Team brief (`curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`); integration file (`enterprise_71a6a9dbc895e9c62ad3bfdd`) |
+| Langfuse web UI, API routes, tRPC, auth, traces/sessions/scores/models/prompts/datasets/eval UX (`web/src/`, `packages/shared/src/`) | Platform & Console, manager Ethan Park | Product for semantics/UX; Security for auth, tenant boundary, user URL/outbound request; Performance & Evals for evaluation behavior | Langfuse repository map (`enterprise_df926424cc402c9cb9aed210`); team brief (`curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`) |
+| Langfuse ingestion, queues, async jobs, exports, retention and evaluation runners (`worker/src/`, shared server code) | Platform & Console + Logan Wright's telemetry organization | SRE for capacity/SLO/incident paths; Security/Privacy for retention or payload changes | Langfuse repository map (`enterprise_df926424cc402c9cb9aed210`); employee directory (`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`) |
+| Langfuse public/server API definitions (`fern/apis/...`) | Platform & Console | Developer-product/API consumers; Product; Security for authentication/rate limits | Langfuse repository map (`enterprise_df926424cc402c9cb9aed210`) |
+| Langfuse enterprise code (`ee/`, `web/src/ee/`) | Explicit enterprise-code owner required | Legal/licensing and Security; no default new-hire write authority | Code manifest (`enterprise_3923c6b386416268c7e7f382`); repository map (`enterprise_df926424cc402c9cb9aed210`) |
+| Build, CI, deployment, production credentials and on-call | SRE/DevOps and Security, not Maya by default | Ethan approves business need; privileged grants require Security and training | New Hire Orientation (`dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982`); access provisioning (`dsid_9fc07b0c73ba41d9b984f6b485670d5d`) |
+
+## Change routing rules
+
+1. Start with the narrowest subsystem owner above; add reviewers whenever a change crosses a row boundary.
+2. Gateway-to-console schema changes require both the LiteLLM gateway contract owner and Langfuse ingestion/console owner, plus Telemetry for payload/fidelity changes.
+3. Auth, RBAC, tenant isolation, secrets, retention, outbound URLs, customer data, or security disclosure always trigger Security review.
+4. Routing/fallback semantics trigger Smart Routing; evaluation semantics trigger Performance & Evals; customer-visible UX triggers Product; deploy/SLO/on-call behavior triggers SRE.
+5. Upstream issues and patches are internally triaged first. Never publish customer data or vulnerability details; upstream maintainers own acceptance, while Redwood owners approve what Redwood may disclose.
+
+## Repository validation baselines
+
+- LiteLLM: focused PR, CLA, test for backend logic, `make lint`, `make test-unit`; UI changes require `npm run test` and `npm run build`; target upstream `litellm_internal_staging`, not `main`. [Contributor guide](/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md) (`enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`).
+- Langfuse: use repository pnpm scripts and local Docker dependencies, test the affected web/shared/worker packages, and apply the repository code/security review checklists. Security reports go privately to `security@langfuse.com`. [Contributor guide](/code/langfuse/CONTRIBUTING.md) (`enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`); [security policy](/code/langfuse/SECURITY.md) (`enterprise_d5cbe5168df3a0be47a0123c`).
+
+## Known gaps
+
+The evidence assigns repositories to teams and names Redwood organization leaders, but it does not provide a complete Redwood path-level CODEOWNERS file for these upstream mirrors. Ethan must confirm named delegates for Langfuse console and ingestion review, the proposed onboarding mentors, and the approver for enterprise-only directories before Maya receives write access.
*** End Patch
